heard: One of the universe's largest black holes has mysteriously vanished. At the center of galaxy, a 2261 BCG, astronomers expected a monster up to 100 billion times the mass of our sun. Instead, Hubble observations showed a bloated core measuring 10,000 light years across with no concentrated peak of starlight. Deep chundra x-ray searches from 1999 and 2004 detected no signs of superheated material falling into a central black hole. In 2018, a team led by Keihin Goltakin of the University of Michigan tried again, but also failed to find anything. The leading theory is that asymmetric gravitational waves from a giant cosmic merger kick the black hole completely out of the galaxy. Today, astronomers are still searching deep space to find this invisible, runaway giant.
